defects.title: API actions reachable with a session but no explicit permission check
defects.detail: 389 action(s) rely on authentication only. Any signed-in user of any role can invoke them. The new API must attach an explicit permission to every route.

defects.title: State-changing operations reachable without authentication via email links
defects.detail: 6 action(s) (indent / purchase-request approve-reject, stock acknowledgement) execute on a URL token alone. Tokens travel in email, in link scanners and in browser history. The replacement keeps an explicit signed, single-use, expiring token endpoint — but scoped to one action, rate limited, and recorded in the audit log.

defects.title: Web app is published as ANYONE_ANONYMOUS with broad OAuth scopes
defects.detail: The deployment is world-readable and executes as the deploying account. All authorisation therefore rests on the in-script token check. The new platform must use per-user authentication with scoped authorisation.

defects.title: Full Drive scope granted to the application
defects.detail: The app holds read/write over the entire Drive of the deploying account, which is far beyond what document generation needs. The replacement uses a scoped object-storage adapter plus per-tenant Google OAuth with least privilege.

defects.title: Configuration and secrets held in PropertiesService script properties
defects.detail: 75 uses of PropertiesService. Script properties are readable by anyone with editor access to the Apps Script project and are not versioned, auditable or rotatable. The replacement stores configuration in the database and secrets in a managed secret store.

defects.title: No tenant isolation: all data lives in one spreadsheet namespace
defects.detail: Every record in the legacy system belongs to a single implicit organisation. There is no tenant_id concept anywhere in the schema, so sharing the application between customers is impossible without a redesign. This is the single largest change in the new platform and is why Part 5 mandates tenant_id on every tenant-owned table.

defects.title: Insufficient critical-section protection
defects.detail: Only 2 LockService usage(s) across 42 files while the app performs thousands of sheet writes, including payroll and invoice numbering. Two simultaneous users can interleave reads and writes. The replacement uses PostgreSQL transactions and row locks.

defects.title: Monolithic single-file frontend
defects.detail: Index.html is 2.14 MB and 23,101 lines with 18 script blocks and 21 style blocks. It cannot be code-split, tree-shaken, unit-tested or cached per-route, and every user downloads the whole application.

defects.title: Silent failure swallowing
defects.detail: 338 empty catch block(s) discard errors without logging. Failures in payroll or invoicing can pass unnoticed. The replacement uses a central exception filter and structured logging with correlation ids.

defects.title: Unstructured console logging in production paths
defects.detail: 16 console.* calls with no redaction layer. Apps Script logs are visible to project editors and may contain employee or client data. The replacement uses a structured logger with a mandatory redaction allow-list that refuses to serialise password, token, bank-account and employee-personal fields.
